seoTitle: Electrical Panel Upgrade in Yardley, PA | 200 Amp Upgrades in Bucks County
seoDescription: Electrical panel and service upgrades in Yardley, PA. 100A to 200A upgrades, PECO coordination, permits and inspection by licensed electricians. Free estimates.
intro: If your breakers trip when two things run at once, or you're planning an EV charger, a heat pump or a finished basement, your panel may be the bottleneck. We upgrade panels and electrical services for Yardley homes every week, from the permit to the final inspection.
summary: Replace an outdated or overloaded electrical panel with a modern 200-amp service. We handle the permit, the PECO disconnect and reconnect, the inspection, and label every circuit when we're done.
imageAlt: Ryan Huck working in a full residential electrical panel
signsTitle: Signs You Need a Panel Upgrade
signsList:
• Breakers trip when the microwave and toaster run together
  • You have a 60 or 100 amp service and want to add major appliances
  • The panel is warm, buzzing, rusty or smells like burning plastic
  • There are no open slots, or the panel is full of tandem breakers
  • It's a Federal Pacific Stab-Lok or Zinsco panel
  • Your home insurer or home inspector flagged the panel
body:
What a Panel Upgrade Involves

Most upgrades in older Yardley homes go from 100 amps to 200 amps. That usually means a new panel, new service entrance cable, a new meter base when the utility requires it, and updated grounding and bonding. We pull the permit with your township, schedule the disconnect and reconnect with PECO, and book the inspection.

On the day of the swap, your power is off for part of the day. We move every circuit to the new panel, replace any breakers that are damaged or wrong for the wire size, and add the protection current code requires. Before we leave, every breaker gets a clear, typed label, so you know what each one controls.

Sometimes a full upgrade isn't needed. If your service is big enough but the panel is out of space, a subpanel may solve the problem for less. If you still have fuses, see our page on fuse box replacement. We'll tell you which option actually fits your house.

What Affects the Cost

The price depends on the size of the new service, whether the meter base and service cable need replacing, where the panel sits in the house, and how many circuits need new breakers or repairs. Moving the panel to a new location costs more than a same-spot swap. Your written estimate spells out all of it before any work starts, so there are no surprises on the invoice.

Breaker Replacement

A breaker that trips for no reason, feels hot or won't reset is telling you something. We find out why it failed first, whether that's a loose connection, an overloaded circuit or a breaker that's simply worn out, then replace it with the breaker your panel is listed for, not just one that fits. Mismatched breakers are one of the most common problems we find in older Bucks County panels.

AFCI Breakers

Arc-fault (AFCI) breakers detect the kind of sparking that starts fires inside walls. Current code requires them on most living-space circuits, so we add them during panel upgrades and remodels. If an AFCI keeps tripping, there's usually a real cause, like a damaged cable or a loose connection, and we track it down instead of swapping in a standard breaker.

Panel Upgrades Around Yardley

A lot of our panel work is in the 1950s and 1960s homes of Levittown and Feasterville, where the original services were never sized for today's appliances. We also upgrade panels in the historic homes of Doylestown, and coordinate with the borough utility on upgrades in Quakertown.
faq:
How long does a panel upgrade take?

The work itself is usually done in one day, with the power off for part of it. Scheduling the PECO reconnect and the inspection can add a few days on either side.

Do I need a permit to replace my electrical panel?

Yes. A panel or service upgrade always needs a permit and an inspection in Pennsylvania. We pull the permit and meet the inspector for you.

Is a 200 amp service enough for an EV charger?

In most homes, yes. We run a load calculation first to confirm there's room for the charger along with your heating, cooking and other large loads.

title: Electrical Subpanel Installation
h1: Electrical Subpanel Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Electrical Subpanel Installation in Yardley, PA | Subpanels in Bucks County
seoDescription: Subpanel installation in Yardley, PA for garages, basements, additions and workshops. Load calculations, permits and clean installs by licensed electricians.
intro: A subpanel gives you room for new circuits without replacing your main panel. It's the right fix when your service has enough capacity but the panel is out of space, or when a garage, basement or addition needs its own set of breakers close to where the power is used.
summary: Add circuits where you need them with a subpanel for a garage, basement, addition or workshop. We check your service capacity first, size the feeder properly and handle the permit and inspection.
imageAlt: Ryan Huck wiring a new breaker panel in a Bucks County basement
signsTitle: When a Subpanel Makes Sense
signsList:
• Your main panel has no open slots, but your service isn't overloaded
  • You're finishing a basement and need several new circuits
  • A detached garage or workshop needs lights, outlets and tools
  • An addition is a long run from the main panel
  • You want space for a future EV charger or generator hookup
body:
How We Install a Subpanel

We start with a load calculation. A subpanel adds space, not capacity, so if your service is already close to its limit, the honest answer may be a panel upgrade instead. When a subpanel fits, we choose its location, size the feeder cable and breaker to match what you'll run on it, and install it with separate ground and neutral bars as the code requires.

For a detached building, the feeder runs underground in conduit at the proper depth, and the building gets its own grounding electrode and a disconnect. Inside the house, we route cable through joists and finished spaces as cleanly as we can and patch only what we have to open. Every new circuit is labeled, and the job is permitted and inspected.

What Affects the Cost

Cost depends mostly on the distance between the main panel and the subpanel, the size of the feeder, whether trenching is involved, and how many circuits you want installed now. A 60-amp subpanel in a basement next to the main panel is a very different job from a 100-amp feed to a barn across the yard. We price it out in writing before we start.

Subpanels and Generators

A subpanel can also make a backup generator simpler. Instead of wiring a transfer switch to every circuit in the house, we can move the essentials, like the furnace, refrigerator, sump pump and a few lights and outlets, to a dedicated subpanel that the generator feeds. It's a common setup for homes that lose power in storms.

Subpanels Around Yardley

We install subpanels for basement finishes in Southampton and Langhorne, and for detached garages and workshops in Warminster and on the larger lots around Washington Crossing. If you're adding a building, our shed and garage wiring page covers the rest of that job.
faq:
Will a subpanel give me more power?

No. It gives you more breaker space. The total power available is still limited by your main service, which is why we run a load calculation before recommending one.

Can a subpanel go in a detached garage?

Yes. A detached building needs its own grounding and a disconnect, and the feeder runs underground in conduit. We handle all of it, including the permit.

How big should my subpanel be?

It depends on what you plan to run. A basement might need 60 amps, while a workshop with welders or a garage with an EV charger may need 100 amps or more.

title: Fuse Box Replacement
h1: Fuse Box Replacement in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Fuse Box Replacement in Yardley, PA | Fuse Box Electrician in Bucks County
seoDescription: Fuse box replacement and fuse changing in Yardley, PA. Convert an old fuse panel to a modern breaker panel with permits and inspection. Licensed electricians.
intro: Fuse boxes did their job for decades, but most can't handle a modern home's electrical load, and many insurers won't cover a house that still has one. We replace fuse boxes with breaker panels across Yardley, and we'll also change a blown fuse safely if that's all you need today.
summary: Replace an old fuse box with a modern circuit breaker panel, or get a blown fuse changed safely. We make sure every fuse is the right size for its wire and upgrade the service when it's due.
signsTitle: Signs Your Fuse Box Needs Attention
signsList:
• Fuses blow regularly, especially in the kitchen or when the AC starts
  • Someone has installed a larger fuse than the circuit's wire can handle
  • There are pennies or foil behind fuses, or the box shows scorch marks
  • Your insurance company or buyer's inspector flagged the fuse box
  • You want to add circuits, and there's no room left
body:
Changing a Blown Fuse the Right Way

A fuse blows to protect the wire behind it. The most dangerous thing we find in older homes is a 20 or 30 amp fuse screwed into a socket meant for 15 amps, because the wire can overheat long before that fuse blows. When we change fuses, we match each one to its wire size and can install tamper-resistant Type S adapters so the wrong size can't go back in. If fuses keep blowing, that's a sign the circuit is overloaded, and the lasting fix is more circuits or a new panel.

Replacing a Fuse Box With a Breaker Panel

Most fuse boxes we replace are on 60 amp services, so the job is usually a full panel and service upgrade to 100 or 200 amps. We pull the permit, coordinate the PECO disconnect, install the new panel and service equipment, move each circuit to a properly sized breaker, and book the inspection. Homes with fuse boxes often have old wiring too, and we'll tell you honestly whether any of it needs rewiring.

What Affects the Cost

A fuse box swap costs more than a breaker-panel swap because the service equipment usually has to change too. The size of the new service, the condition of the existing wiring and the number of circuits all affect the price. Your written estimate covers everything.

What to Expect on Replacement Day

Your power will be off for most of the day while we swap the equipment. We'll tell you in advance, so you can plan around refrigerators, medical devices and work from home, and we restore power as soon as the utility reconnects.

Fuse Boxes Around Yardley

We still find fuse boxes in older homes along Radcliffe Street in Bristol, in Morrisville twins and rowhomes, and in older borough homes in Sellersville and Perkasie.
faq:
Is it safe to keep my fuse box?

A fuse box with correctly sized fuses isn't dangerous by itself. The problems are oversized fuses, overloaded circuits and old wiring, which is why we inspect it before recommending anything.

Will my insurance company care about my fuse box?

Many insurers charge more for homes with fuse boxes or won't write a policy at all. Replacing it usually solves that problem.

Can you just change a blown fuse?

Yes. We'll replace it with the correct size and check why it blew, so you know whether the circuit needs more work.

title: Home Rewiring
h1: Home Rewiring in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Home Rewiring in Yardley, PA | Knob-and-Tube Replacement in Bucks County
seoDescription: Whole and partial home rewiring in Yardley, PA. Replace knob-and-tube, cloth and ungrounded wiring with minimal wall damage. Licensed electricians.
intro: Older wiring wasn't built for today's electrical loads, and after 60 or 80 years its insulation can crack and crumble. We rewire older homes around Yardley room by room or all at once, fishing new cable through existing walls so you're not left with a gutted house.
summary: Replace knob-and-tube, cloth-insulated or ungrounded wiring in older homes, room by room or all at once. We fish new cable through existing walls wherever we can, so you get new wiring with as little patching as possible.
imageAlt: Ryan Huck updating an older home's electrical panel
signsTitle: Signs Your Home Needs Rewiring
signsList:
• You have knob-and-tube wiring, or cloth-covered cable that crumbles when touched
  • Most outlets are two-prong, with no ground wire
  • Lights dim or flicker when appliances start
  • Outlets or switch plates feel warm
  • Your insurer won't cover the house until the wiring is replaced
  • You're remodeling and the walls are already open
body:
How We Rewire a House

We start with a walkthrough to map what's in the walls and what you want the finished house to have: more outlets, dedicated kitchen circuits, grounded receptacles, better lighting. Then we plan cable routes through attics, basements and existing wall cavities. Most rewires need only small, neat access holes rather than open walls, and we can arrange drywall and plaster patching when we're done.

New wiring is grounded throughout and gets arc-fault and ground-fault protection where current code requires it. We usually rewire one area at a time, so you keep power in the rest of the house while we work. Many rewires include a panel upgrade, since an old fuse box or undersized panel can't support the new circuits.

Partial Rewiring

Not every house needs a full rewire. If the problem is a few ungrounded circuits, ground wire installation may be enough. If your house was built in the late 1960s or early 1970s, check whether it has aluminum branch wiring; our aluminum wiring page covers that separately.

What Affects the Cost

Square footage, number of stories, plaster versus drywall, attic and basement access, and how many circuits and outlets you want all shape the price. We give you a written estimate by room or area, so you can phase the work if that fits your budget better.

Living in the House During a Rewire

We plan the work so the kitchen, a bathroom and bedrooms stay usable each night. Furniture gets moved away from the walls we're working on and covered, and we clean up dust at the end of each day. You'll always know which rooms we're in next.

Upgrades Without a Full Rewire

Not every older house needs new wiring throughout. Often the right answer is a set of targeted upgrades: grounded three-prong outlets, a few new circuits for the kitchen and home office, USB and GFCI outlets where they're needed, and better lighting. We'll tell you honestly whether your wiring can be updated in place or needs replacing.

Grounding Ungrounded Outlets

Two-prong outlets, or three-prong outlets with no ground behind them, are common in homes built before the 1960s. We run new ground wires where we can, add GFCI protection where code allows it instead, and check the grounding electrode and the bonding of water and gas pipes. Good grounding is also what lets surge protection and sensitive electronics work as designed.

Rewiring Around Yardley

We rewire historic homes in Doylestown and New Hope, and older twins and singles in Quakertown and Morrisville, where knob-and-tube and early cloth-insulated cable are still common.
faq:
How long does it take to rewire a house?

A typical single-family home takes one to two weeks, depending on size and access. We work in sections so you're not without power the whole time.

Do I have to move out while you rewire?

Usually not. We work one area at a time and restore power at the end of each day.

Is knob-and-tube wiring dangerous?

It was well made, but after decades the insulation breaks down, it has no ground, and it was never meant to be buried in insulation. Most insurers now want it replaced.

title: Aluminum Wiring Replacement
h1: Aluminum Wiring Replacement in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Aluminum Wiring Replacement in Yardley, PA | AlumiConn Repair in Bucks County
seoDescription: Aluminum wiring repair and replacement in Yardley, PA. Safe copper pigtail repairs or full rewiring for 1960s–70s homes. Licensed, insured electricians.
intro: Some homes built in the mid-1960s to mid-1970s were wired with single-strand aluminum branch circuits. The wire itself isn't the problem; the connections are. Aluminum expands, contracts and oxidizes at outlets and switches, which can make them overheat. We repair and replace aluminum wiring in Yardley-area homes with methods the industry recognizes as safe.
summary: Homes wired with single-strand aluminum in the 1960s and 70s can overheat at outlets and switches. We make every connection safe with approved copper pigtail connectors, or replace the aluminum wiring entirely.
signsTitle: Signs of an Aluminum Wiring Problem
signsList:
• Your home was built between roughly 1965 and 1975
  • The cable jacket is stamped "AL" or "Aluminum," or the wire is silver-colored
  • Outlets or switch plates feel warm
  • Lights flicker, or outlets work intermittently
  • You smell burning plastic near an outlet or switch
  • A home inspection flagged aluminum branch wiring
body:
Repair or Replace?

There are two lasting fixes. The first is to keep the aluminum wiring and make every connection safe by attaching a short copper pigtail with a connector made for the job, such as AlumiConn or COPALUM. Every outlet, switch, light, junction box and panel connection in the house gets treated, not just the ones that look bad. The second is a full rewire with copper, which costs more but removes the aluminum completely.

We'll inspect your system and explain both options. What we won't do is use standard twist-on connectors or "CO/ALR" devices as a whole-house fix; they aren't a substitute for proper remediation.

Our Remediation Process

We work circuit by circuit, opening every box, checking the wire for damage from past overheating, and installing the approved connectors with the right tools. Damaged devices get replaced, and outlets and switches are replaced with new ones where needed. When we're done, you get documentation of the work, which buyers, inspectors and insurers often ask for.

What Affects the Cost

The number of connection points drives the price: every outlet, switch, fixture and junction box counts. A full copper rewire depends on the house's size and access. We'll give you written prices for both approaches.

Why Standard Connectors Aren't Enough

Aluminum and copper expand at different rates, and aluminum forms an oxide layer that doesn't conduct well. Ordinary twist-on connectors and the screw terminals on standard devices can loosen and heat up as they cycle. The connectors we use are designed and tested for aluminum-to-copper connections and are installed with the correct tools, which is why they're recognized as a permanent repair.

Aluminum Wiring Around Yardley

We find aluminum branch wiring in homes and townhouses built during that era in Bensalem and Lower Makefield, and often fix it as part of code corrections before a sale in Langhorne.

Aluminum wiring can be made safe when every connection is properly remediated. Untreated connections are the fire risk.

Will my insurance cover a house with aluminum wiring?

Some insurers won't, or require proof of remediation. Our documentation of the repair usually satisfies them.

Can I just replace the outlets with aluminum-rated ones?

That isn't a complete fix. Every connection in the system needs attention, including fixtures, junction boxes and the panel.

title: Whole House Surge Protection
h1: Whole House Surge Protection in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Whole House Surge Protection in Yardley, PA | Surge Protectors, Bucks County
seoDescription: Whole house surge protector installation in Yardley, PA. Protect appliances, HVAC and electronics at the panel. Licensed electricians, free estimates.
intro: Plug-in power strips only protect what's plugged into them. A whole-house surge protector mounts at your electrical panel and protects every circuit, including the furnace, air conditioner, refrigerator, washer and all the electronics built into modern appliances.
summary: A surge protector installed at your electrical panel protects everything in the house, from the furnace and fridge to TVs and computers, against surges from lightning, the utility and your own large appliances.
signsTitle: Good Reasons to Add Surge Protection
signsList:
• You've lost a TV, router, garage door opener or appliance board after a storm
  • Your home has expensive HVAC, a generator, solar or an EV charger
  • Lights briefly brighten or flicker when large appliances cycle
  • You're upgrading or replacing your panel
  • You work from home and rely on your computer and network
body:
Where Surges Come From

Lightning gets the attention, but most surges start closer to home: utility switching, tree limbs on lines, and large motors in your own house turning on and off. Each surge wears on electronic circuit boards a little, which is why appliances sometimes die early for no clear reason. A panel-mounted protector diverts that excess voltage to ground before it reaches your circuits.

How We Install It

We install a surge protective device in or beside your panel on a dedicated breaker, keeping the leads as short as possible so it reacts fast. We check your grounding and bonding while we're there, because a surge protector is only as good as the ground it dumps energy into. If your grounding needs work, see our page on ground wire installation and repair.

Newer editions of the electrical code require surge protection whenever a service is upgraded or replaced, so we include it in every panel upgrade. For the most protection, we recommend pairing the whole-house device with quality plug-in protectors for computers and home theaters.

What Affects the Cost

The protector's rating, your panel type and whether a breaker space is available all affect the price. Most installs take about an hour.

Signs Your Home Has Been Hit by Surges

Surge damage isn't always dramatic. Watch for electronics that fail after storms, garage door openers and furnace control boards that need replacing more often than they should, and LED bulbs that burn out early. Those are common signs of repeated small surges. A whole-house protector won't repair damage that's already happened, but it can prevent the next round.

Surge Protection Around Yardley

Homes near the river in New Hope and Washington Crossing, and anywhere with overhead lines through the trees, see more than their share of storm surges. We also add protection during panel upgrades in Chalfont.
faq:
Does a whole-house surge protector stop lightning?

Nothing stops a direct lightning strike. A surge protector handles the far more common surges from nearby strikes, the utility and your own appliances.

How long does a surge protector last?

Most last many years, but they wear with each surge they absorb. Many models have an indicator light that shows when they need replacing.

Do I still need power strips?

For computers and home theaters, a good plug-in protector adds a second layer. The whole-house unit protects everything else.

h1: Electrical Repair & Troubleshooting in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Electrical Repair & Troubleshooting in Yardley, PA | Bucks County Electrician
seoDescription: Electrical repair and troubleshooting in Yardley, PA. Dead outlets, tripping breakers, flickering lights and buzzing switches found and fixed.
intro: When part of your house loses power, a breaker won't stay on, or the lights flicker for no clear reason, you need someone who finds the cause, not someone who starts replacing parts. We troubleshoot and repair electrical problems in Yardley-area homes and small businesses every day.
summary: Dead outlets, tripping breakers, flickering lights, buzzing switches and half-working circuits, tracked down methodically and fixed properly. We find the cause instead of guessing, and explain what we found.
imageAlt: Testing a kitchen outlet with a voltage tester to find a fault
signsTitle: Problems We Fix Every Week
signsList:
• Outlets or a whole room that suddenly stopped working
  • Breakers or GFCIs that trip and won't reset
  • Lights that flicker, dim or buzz
  • Switches or outlets that are warm, loose or crackle when used
  • A burning smell, scorch marks or a shock from a switch or appliance
  • Power that works on some outlets on a circuit but not others
body:
How We Troubleshoot

Electrical problems follow the wiring, so we start at the panel and work outward. We test voltage and continuity, check each device on the affected circuit, and look for the usual suspects: a loose connection at a push-in "backstab" outlet, a tripped GFCI in another room that feeds the circuit, a failed splice in a junction box, or a nail through a cable. Once we find the fault, we explain it, give you the price to fix it and make the repair.

If the problem is a worn breaker, see circuit breaker replacement. If it's worn or damaged devices, we replace switches and outlets. Flickering fixtures often have their own causes, covered on our lighting repair page.

When It Can't Wait

Turn off the circuit at the panel and call right away if you see sparks or smoke, smell burning plastic, feel heat at a switch or outlet, or get a shock. Don't reset a breaker that trips immediately. Call 215-906-4634 and we'll tell you how to make things safe until we get there.

What Affects the Cost

Most repairs are straightforward once the problem is found. The time it takes to locate a fault, the parts involved and access to the wiring drive the price. We tell you what we found and what it costs before we fix it.

Problems That Come Back

If you've had the same breaker trip or the same outlet fail more than once, the earlier fix probably treated a symptom. We look for the root cause, such as a shared neutral, an overloaded circuit or a failing splice, so you don't have to call again.

Repairs Around Yardley

We handle repair calls across Morrisville, Bristol and Warminster, and for small businesses along the Route 1 and Street Road corridors.
faq:
Why did half the outlets in my room stop working?

Often a tripped GFCI elsewhere on the circuit, or a loose connection at the last working outlet. We trace it and fix the connection.

Is a flickering light dangerous?

A bulb or dimmer issue isn't, but flicker across several rooms can mean a loose connection at the panel or service. That needs a look soon.

Do you charge to diagnose the problem?

No. Diagnosis and the quote are free. We find the problem, explain it and give you a written price before we fix anything.

seoTitle: Electrical Inspections & Maintenance in Yardley, PA | Bucks County Safety Checks
seoDescription: Electrical maintenance and safety inspections in Yardley, PA: panel checks, connection tightening, GFCI and AFCI tests and smoke alarm checks.
intro: Electrical systems don't need much attention, but they do need some. An electrical inspection catches loose connections, worn devices and missing protection before they turn into a dead circuit or a fire. We inspect and maintain electrical systems for homes and small businesses around Yardley.
summary: A thorough check of your home's electrical system: panel inspection, tightening connections, testing GFCI and AFCI protection, smoke and CO alarms, and a written list of anything that needs attention.
imageAlt: Tightening connections inside an electrical panel during an inspection
signsTitle: Good Times to Schedule a Check
signsList:
• You just bought a home, or you're about to sell one
  • The house is 25 or more years old and hasn't been looked at
  • You've added large appliances, an EV or a hot tub
  • After a storm, flood or lightning strike nearby
  • Before a remodel, so you know what you're working with
body:
What We Check

We open the panel and look at the breakers, the bus bar, and the main, neutral and ground connections, and tighten terminations where needed. We check for overheating, corrosion and double-tapped breakers. We test every GFCI and AFCI, check a sample of outlets for polarity and grounding, and look at exposed wiring in the basement, attic and garage.

We also test your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and note any that are missing or past their replacement date. You get a written list of what we found, sorted into safety items, code items and nice-to-haves, with prices.

Small Business Maintenance

For small offices and shops, we check panels, emergency and exit lighting, outdoor lighting, and dedicated circuits for equipment. We can schedule regular visits so problems are caught between busy seasons.

What Happens Next

Most visits end with nothing urgent and a few small fixes we can take care of the same day. If we find something bigger, like a panel with a known failure history or ungrounded circuits, we explain the options and give you a written price. If you're preparing for a sale, the code corrections section below covers the items inspectors flag most often. Adding a whole-house surge protector is a common upgrade after a maintenance check.

For Older Homes and New Owners

In homes more than 40 years old, we pay extra attention to aluminum or cloth-insulated wiring, panels with known failure histories, and past additions that may not have been done to code. For new homeowners, a maintenance visit is a good way to learn where the panel is, what each circuit feeds and how to reset GFCIs and AFCIs. We'll label anything that isn't clearly marked while we're there.

Code Corrections After a Home Inspection

If you're buying or selling, the inspector's report usually lists electrical items: double-tapped breakers, missing GFCIs, open junction boxes, ungrounded outlets or a panel with a known failure history. We fix them, pull a permit where one is needed and give you documentation for the buyer, seller or lender. Buyers can have us review the report before their negotiation deadline and get real prices to work with.

Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms

Smoke alarms last about ten years, and many CO alarms less. We install hardwired, interconnected smoke and CO alarms with battery backup where code requires them, replace units past their date, and fix alarms that chirp or go off for no reason. In older homes we fish the new wiring through finished walls with as little patching as possible.

Maintenance Around Yardley

We do inspections for new homeowners in Newtown and Morrisville, and maintenance for small businesses in Langhorne.

How often should my home's electrical system be inspected?

For most homes, every few years, and any time you buy a house, add major loads or notice a problem.

What's the most common thing you find?

GFCI outlets that no longer trip when tested, smoke alarms past their ten-year life, and loose connections in the panel.

Is this the same as a home inspection?

No. A home inspector looks at the whole house; we go deeper into the electrical system and can fix what we find.

title: Dedicated Circuit Installation
h1: Dedicated Circuit Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Dedicated Circuit Installation in Yardley, PA | New Circuits in Bucks County
seoDescription: Dedicated circuit installation in Yardley, PA for appliances, space heaters, home offices, freezers, sump pumps and equipment. 120V and 240V circuits.
intro: If a breaker trips every time the microwave, space heater or treadmill runs with something else, that appliance probably needs a circuit of its own. We install dedicated circuits in Yardley homes and businesses so each load gets the power it needs without taking down the rest of the room.
summary: Give appliances and equipment their own circuit so they stop tripping breakers: microwaves, refrigerators, freezers, sump pumps, space heaters, home offices, gym equipment and 240-volt tools.
imageAlt: Replacing a kitchen outlet beside the range
signsTitle: Signs You Need a Dedicated Circuit
signsList:
• A breaker trips when a particular appliance runs with anything else
  • Lights dim when the appliance starts up
  • You're adding a freezer, wine fridge or second refrigerator
  • You need a reliable circuit for a sump pump or medical equipment
  • You're setting up a home office, gym, workshop or window AC
body:
What Gets a Dedicated Circuit

Code requires dedicated circuits for many built-in appliances, including dishwashers, disposals, built-in microwaves, and the washer and furnace. Beyond the rules, anything that draws a lot of power for a long time benefits from its own circuit: space heaters, window air conditioners, freezers, gym equipment and computer setups. Sump pumps and freezers get their own circuit so an unrelated trip doesn't leave you with a flooded basement or spoiled food.

120-Volt and 240-Volt Circuits

Most household equipment runs on 120-volt, 15 or 20 amp circuits. Larger equipment like ranges, dryers, water heaters, welders, air compressors, mini-splits and EV chargers needs a 240-volt circuit sized to the equipment. Our appliance wiring page covers those hookups, and EV charger installation has its own page.

How We Install It

We confirm your panel has space and capacity, size the wire and breaker for the load, and run the new circuit by the cleanest route, often from the basement or attic with a small opening for the new outlet. We add the ground-fault or arc-fault protection the location requires, label the breaker and test the circuit under load. If the panel is full or near capacity, we'll talk through a subpanel or panel upgrade.

What Affects the Cost

Distance from the panel, the circuit's size, how hard the route is, and the type of breaker required all shape the price. A new 20 amp outlet near the panel is a quick job; a 240-volt run to a far corner of the house takes longer.

Appliance Hookups

Ranges, cooktops, wall ovens, dryers, water heaters, dishwashers, disposals and built-in microwaves each need a circuit sized for that appliance and the right connection at the end of it. We wire new appliances, handle gas-to-electric and induction conversions, and check that the cord, receptacle and breaker all match the manufacturer's requirements.

Kitchen Remodels

A remodel is the best time to get kitchen wiring right. Code calls for at least two 20-amp countertop circuits, GFCI protection, and dedicated circuits for the dishwasher, disposal, microwave and refrigerator. We plan island power and range circuits alongside recessed and under-cabinet lighting, and work around your contractor's schedule.

Dedicated Circuits Around Yardley

We add circuits for workshops and home offices in Warminster, and split overloaded circuits in the original homes of Levittown and Fairless Hills.
faq:
Does my refrigerator need its own circuit?

It's strongly recommended, and often required in new kitchens. A shared circuit can trip and leave your food warm.

Can a space heater run on a regular outlet?

It can, but a 1,500-watt heater uses most of a 15-amp circuit by itself. That's the classic cause of tripping in bedrooms and offices.

Do I need a permit for a new circuit?

Yes, a new circuit generally needs a permit. We handle it.

title: Switch & Outlet Installation
h1: Switch & Outlet Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Switch & Outlet Installation in Yardley, PA | Outlet Repair in Bucks County
seoDescription: Switch and outlet installation and replacement in Yardley, PA. New outlets, USB outlets, worn or warm switches replaced, tamper-resistant outlets. Licensed.
intro: Outlets and switches get used thousands of times, and eventually they wear out. We add new outlets where you need them and replace worn, loose or damaged switches and outlets throughout Yardley-area homes, fixing the connections behind them while we're at it.
summary: Add outlets where you need them and replace worn, loose, cracked or warm switches and outlets. We install USB and tamper-resistant outlets and fix the loose connections behind flickering switches.
imageAlt: Installing a new outlet on a kitchen backsplash
signsTitle: Signs It's Time to Replace or Add
signsList:
• Plugs fall out of the outlet or feel loose
  • A switch or outlet is cracked, warm or discolored
  • A switch crackles, sparks or has to be jiggled to work
  • You're running extension cords to reach an outlet
  • Outlets are two-prong or painted over
  • You want USB or USB-C charging built into the wall
body:
Replacing Worn Switches and Outlets

When we replace a device, we don't just swap it. We check the box, the wire and the connections. Many older outlets were wired with push-in "backstab" connections that loosen over time and cause flickering, intermittent power and heat. We move those connections to the screw terminals or use quality back-wire devices, and replace any damaged wire ends. New outlets in homes are tamper-resistant, which keeps kids from pushing objects into the slots.

If a switch is warm or flickers, that's a sign of a loose connection or a device that's failing, and it should be fixed soon. See electrical repair and troubleshooting if the problem is on more than one device.

Adding New Outlets and Switches

We add outlets behind TVs and beds, along kitchen counters, in hallways, garages and home offices, usually by fishing wire from the basement or attic and cutting only a small opening for the new box. We can add switches for lights that only have a pull chain, and install combination switch-and-outlet devices where space is tight. Moving an existing outlet or switch is covered on our switch and outlet relocation page. For dimmers, see dimmer switch installation.

What Affects the Cost

Replacing devices is priced per device and goes quickly when several are done at once. New outlets depend on access and distance from a circuit with capacity.

Moving Outlets and Switches

Outlets end up in the wrong place: behind a new wall-mounted TV, under new cabinets, or on the hinge side of a door. We move them where they make sense, close up the old boxes to code and keep wall repairs as small as possible.

Dimmer Switches

Most flicker and buzz problems with LED bulbs come from a dimmer that wasn't made for them. We install LED-compatible and smart dimmers matched to your fixtures, including dimming from more than one location.

3-Way and 4-Way Switches

Want to control a light from the top and bottom of the stairs, or from both ends of a hallway? We add new switch locations and fix 3-way circuits that only work from one side, usually without opening more than the switch boxes.

Outlet and Switch Work Around Yardley

We replace outlets and switches throughout Bensalem and Morrisville, and add outlets to older rooms in Sellersville that were built with only one or two.
faq:
Why do my plugs fall out of the outlet?

The outlet's internal contacts are worn. It should be replaced, since a loose connection can overheat.

Are USB outlets worth it?

For bedsides, kitchens and desks, yes. They free up plug space and charge devices without adapters.

Can I replace a switch myself?

Many people do, but if the switch was warm or sparking, have the box and wiring checked, because the problem may be behind the switch.

title: GFCI Outlet Installation
h1: GFCI Outlet Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: GFCI Outlet Installation in Yardley, PA | GFCI Outlets in Bucks County
seoDescription: GFCI outlet installation in Yardley, PA for kitchens, bathrooms, garages, basements, laundry and outdoors. Code corrections and GFCI troubleshooting.
intro: A GFCI outlet shuts off power in a fraction of a second when it senses electricity taking a path it shouldn't, such as through a person standing near water. It's one of the most effective shock-prevention devices ever made, and one of the most common items on Yardley home inspection reports.
summary: Ground-fault (GFCI) protection for kitchens, bathrooms, laundry areas, garages, basements and outdoor outlets. We install GFCI outlets and breakers where code requires and fix GFCIs that won't reset.
imageAlt: Testing a bathroom outlet with a receptacle tester
signsTitle: Where You Need GFCI Protection
signsList:
• Kitchen countertop outlets and outlets near any sink
  • Bathrooms and laundry areas
  • Garages and unfinished basements
  • All outdoor outlets, including decks and porches
  • Near pools, hot tubs and wet bars
  • Anywhere a home inspector flagged "missing GFCI"
body:
GFCI Outlets vs. GFCI Breakers

There are two ways to protect a circuit. A GFCI outlet protects itself and every outlet wired after it on the circuit. A GFCI breaker in the panel protects the whole circuit from its source, which is useful when outlets are hard to reach, when a circuit feeds outdoor outlets, or for equipment like hot tubs. We'll choose the right method for each location, and label protected outlets downstream so you know where to reset.

Installing and Testing

We identify the first outlet on each circuit, install GFCI protection there or at the panel, and test every outlet it covers. GFCIs can also protect ungrounded three-prong outlets when a ground wire isn't available, labeled "No equipment ground" as the code requires; see ground wire installation for a permanent ground. For outdoor locations, see outdoor outlet installation. In bathrooms, we often pair GFCI work with bathroom fixture wiring.

GFCIs That Trip or Won't Reset

A GFCI that trips often may have found a real problem, such as moisture in an outdoor box, a worn appliance or damaged wiring. A GFCI that won't reset may have failed, or may have no power coming in. We find the cause. GFCIs also wear out and should be tested monthly with the test button.

What Affects the Cost

GFCI outlets are affordable; GFCI breakers cost more. Most homes need only a handful, placed at the start of each circuit.

Outdoor Outlets

Every outdoor outlet needs GFCI protection, a weather-resistant receptacle and an in-use cover that stays closed while something is plugged in. We add outlets for decks, patios and porches, holiday lights, landscape lighting transformers, pool equipment and yard tools, and replace cracked or rusted ones. An outdoor GFCI that trips every time it rains usually has water getting past a worn cover or a damaged receptacle, and we fix the cause instead of just resetting it.

GFCI Work Around Yardley

We add GFCI protection as part of code corrections before sales in Southampton and Langhorne, and in basements and garages in Feasterville.
faq:
Why did several outlets stop working at once?

Often a GFCI in another room, the garage or outside has tripped. Press its reset button. If it won't reset, call us.

How often should I test my GFCIs?

Once a month. Press test, confirm power goes off, then press reset.

Do GFCI outlets wear out?

Yes. Most last many years, but a GFCI that no longer trips when tested should be replaced.

h1: Ceiling Fan Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Ceiling Fan Installation in Yardley, PA | Fan Installers in Bucks County
seoDescription: Ceiling fan installation in Yardley, PA. Replace a light with a fan, add fans to rooms with no fixture, fan-rated boxes, separate fan and light control.
intro: A ceiling fan makes a room more comfortable in summer and helps move warm air in winter. We install ceiling fans across Yardley, from simple fixture swaps to fans in rooms that were built with no ceiling wiring at all.
summary: Ceiling fans installed securely on fan-rated boxes, whether you're replacing a light fixture or adding a fan to a room with no ceiling wiring. Separate fan and light control, remotes and high-ceiling downrods.
signsTitle: When to Call an Electrician for a Fan
signsList:
• You're replacing a light fixture with a fan
  • The room has no ceiling fixture, only a switched outlet
  • You want the fan and light on separate switches
  • The fan wobbles, hums or the light flickers
  • The ceiling is high or sloped
body:
Fan-Rated Boxes Matter

A ceiling fan is heavy and it moves, and a standard light fixture box isn't built to hold it. Every fan we install is mounted to a fan-rated box or brace secured to the ceiling framing. When we replace a light with a fan, we check the existing box and replace it if it isn't rated, usually without opening the ceiling. That's the difference between a fan that runs quietly for years and one that wobbles or works loose.

Adding a Fan Where There's No Fixture

Many older homes, especially 1950s homes in lower Bucks County, have bedrooms with no ceiling fixture. We run a new switch leg from the wall switch to the ceiling through the attic, install a fan-rated box and wire the fan. If you want the fan and light on separate wall switches, we run the extra conductor while we're there. Remote and wall-control kits are an option when adding wire isn't practical. For light-only fixtures, see ceiling light installation.

Assembly, Balance and Setup

We assemble the fan, set the blade pitch, balance it so it runs without wobble and set the direction for the season. On high or sloped ceilings, we install the right downrod length and slope adapter. If you're ventilating a hot attic rather than cooling a room, see attic fan installation.

What Affects the Cost

Replacing a fixture with a fan is the quickest job. Adding a new switch leg, separate fan and light control, high ceilings and heavy fans take more time. We quote the whole job, including the box.

Porch and Outdoor Fans

Covered porches and patios need fans rated for damp or wet locations, and they're usually mounted to boxes that can handle outdoor conditions. We'll check the rating and wire them with GFCI protection where required.

Attic Fans

A powered attic ventilator pulls hot, humid air out of the attic in summer. We install gable fans, wire roof-mounted units, add thermostat and humidistat controls, and repair attic fans that have stopped running.

Bathroom Exhaust Fans and Fixtures

Bathroom fans need to vent outside, not into the attic, and work best on a timer or humidity sensor. During bathroom updates we also wire vanity lights, wet-rated shower lights, heated floors, towel warmers and the GFCI protection every bathroom outlet needs.

Ceiling Fans Around Yardley

We install a lot of ceiling fans in the original bedrooms of Fairless Hills, Levittown and Feasterville homes, and on porches in Southampton.
faq:
Can I put a ceiling fan where my light fixture is?

Usually, if the box is fan-rated or can be replaced with one. We check and upgrade the box as part of the install.

Can the fan and light be on separate switches?

Yes, if there's an extra conductor, which we can run. Otherwise a remote or smart control is an option.

Why does my fan wobble?

Usually unbalanced blades or a loose mount. We balance the fan and check the box.

h1: Hot Tub Electrical Hookup in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Hot Tub Electrical Hookup in Yardley, PA | Spa Wiring in Bucks County
seoDescription: Hot tub and spa electrical hookup in Yardley, PA. 240V circuit, GFCI disconnect, bonding, permits and inspection by licensed electricians. Free estimates.
intro: A hot tub needs a dedicated 240-volt circuit, a GFCI-protected disconnect in the right place, and proper bonding. We wire hot tubs and swim spas for Yardley-area homeowners, from the panel to the final inspection, so your tub is ready to fill on delivery day.
summary: Complete hot tub and swim spa wiring: a 240-volt circuit sized to the tub, a GFCI-protected disconnect at the required distance, bonding, the permit and the inspection.
imageAlt: Testing a pool pump timer and weatherproof outdoor outlet on a post
signsTitle: What Your Hot Tub Needs
signsList:
• A 240-volt circuit sized to the tub, commonly 40, 50 or 60 amps
  • A GFCI-protected disconnect within sight of the tub and at least five feet away
  • Bonding of the tub's metal parts and nearby metal
  • Space and capacity in your panel
  • A permit and inspection
body:
Planning the Location

Before the tub arrives, we look at where it will sit, where the panel is and how the circuit will get there. Most runs go underground in conduit or along the house exterior. The disconnect has to be within sight of the tub but at least five feet from its inside wall, so someone in the water can't reach it. We also check overhead lines, since hot tubs have required clearances from them.

Installation

We run the circuit from the panel with wire sized for the tub's amperage and the distance, install the GFCI disconnect, and connect the tub according to the manufacturer's instructions. The tub's metal parts are bonded as the code requires. After the inspection, we power it up with you and confirm the GFCI trips when tested. If your panel lacks capacity or space, we'll explain options including a panel upgrade.

Plug-In Tubs and Swim Spas

Some small "plug and play" tubs run on a 120-volt outlet, but they still need a dedicated, GFCI-protected outdoor outlet in the right place. Swim spas usually need larger circuits and sometimes two. For in-ground pools, see pool electrical wiring.

What Affects the Cost

The distance from the panel, the tub's amperage, trenching or surface routing, and panel capacity drive the price. We'll give you a written estimate before delivery day.

Before Delivery Day

Order the tub, then call us with the model. We'll confirm its electrical requirements from the manufacturer's manual, plan the circuit and disconnect location, pull the permit and schedule the work so the wiring is inspected before the tub arrives. That way it can be filled and running the day it's set. If the tub is going on a deck, we'll plan the route with your deck builder.

Pool Wiring

In-ground and above-ground pools need circuits for the pump, filter and heater, GFCI protection, pool lighting and equipotential bonding, which ties the pool's metal parts together so there's no shock hazard in the water. Pools are inspected more closely than almost anything else we wire, and we handle the permit and the inspection.

Hot Tubs Around Yardley

We wire hot tubs and pools on decks and patios throughout Newtown and Warminster, and on larger properties around Washington Crossing.
faq:
How far does the disconnect need to be from the hot tub?

At least five feet from the inside wall of the tub, and within sight of it.

What size breaker does my hot tub need?

It depends on the model. Most need 40 to 60 amps. We follow the manufacturer's specifications.

Do I need a permit for a hot tub?

Yes. The circuit and disconnect need a permit and an inspection.

title: Basement Wiring
h1: Basement Wiring in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Basement Wiring in Yardley, PA | Finished Basements in Bucks County
seoDescription: Basement wiring in Yardley, PA for finished basements: circuits, outlets, recessed lighting, smoke alarms, subpanels, permits and inspections.
intro: A finished basement is one of the best ways to add living space, and the electrical is a big part of getting it right. We wire basements around Yardley, from planning the layout to passing the final inspection.
summary: Complete electrical for finished basements: circuits, outlets, recessed lighting, AFCI and GFCI protection, smoke alarms, sump pump circuits and a subpanel if your main panel is full.
signsTitle: What a Finished Basement Usually Needs
signsList:
• Outlets along every wall, plus for the TV and bar area
  • Recessed lighting on dimmers, zoned by area
  • A dedicated circuit for the sump pump, freezer or gym
  • Smoke and CO alarms tied into your existing system
  • Room in the panel for all of it
body:
Planning the Layout

We walk the space with you and your contractor and plan it room by room: outlets for furniture and TVs, lighting zones, a bathroom or bar, and a home office or gym. Code sets minimum outlet spacing and requires arc-fault protection for living areas and ground-fault protection for unfinished areas, bathrooms and wet bars. We plan for all of it up front.

Lighting a Basement

Basements are dark, and lighting makes or breaks the space. Recessed lights work well under low ceilings; we use slim LED fixtures that fit around ductwork and pipes and put them on dimmers by zone.

The Panel and Protected Circuits

Basement finishes add a lot of circuits, and many older main panels are full. A subpanel in the basement is often the simplest way to add space. Sump pumps and freezers get their own circuits so an unrelated trip can't take them down. New smoke and CO alarms are required and interconnected with the rest of the house.

What Affects the Cost

Square footage, the number of rooms, lighting count, bathrooms or bars and whether a subpanel is needed shape the price. We quote from your plan.

Damp Basements

If your basement gets damp, we'll address it in the plan. Outlets in unfinished areas need GFCI protection, fixtures in damp spots need the right rating, and wiring should stay clear of areas that take on water. Sump pumps get their own circuit, and we can add a battery backup outlet for them. We'll also make sure the panel and any subpanel stay accessible, with the clear working space in front of them that the code requires, even after the finish work is done.

Additions, Attics and Remodels

The same planning applies to any new living space: additions, attic conversions, sunrooms and major remodels. We lay out circuits, outlets, switches and lighting around how you'll use the room, coordinate with your builder, and handle the rough-in, trim-out and inspections.

New Construction

For new homes we also install the service and panel and provide temporary power during the build, working to your builder's schedule from rough-in to the final inspection.

Basement Wiring Around Yardley

We wire basement finishes and additions throughout Feasterville, Langhorne and Warminster.
faq:
Do I need a permit to finish my basement's electrical?

Yes. New circuits and wiring need a permit with rough and final inspections.

How many outlets does a basement need?

Code requires outlets along the walls so no point is more than six feet from one. We usually add more for TVs, desks and bars.

Can you wire around existing ductwork and pipes?

Yes. We use slim LED fixtures and plan routes around mechanicals.

title: Shed, Garage & Barn Wiring
h1: Shed & Garage Wiring in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Shed & Garage Wiring in Yardley, PA | Garage Power in Bucks County
seoDescription: Shed and garage wiring in Yardley, PA. Power to detached garages and sheds, underground feeders, subpanels, lighting, outlets and EV chargers. Licensed.
intro: A shed or detached garage without power is just storage. With lights and outlets it's a workshop, a gym or a place to charge the car. We run power to detached garages, sheds and workshops around Yardley, from a single circuit to a full subpanel.
summary: Power for detached garages, sheds and workshops: underground feeders, subpanels, lighting, outlets, 240-volt tool circuits and EV charger circuits, permitted and inspected.
signsTitle: What Your Garage or Shed Might Need
signsList:
• Lights and a few outlets for tools and a fridge
  • 240-volt circuits for a compressor, welder or table saw
  • An EV charger in a detached garage
  • A subpanel for a workshop or finished space
  • Replacing an old extension-cord or overhead-wire setup
body:
Getting Power to the Building

Most detached buildings are fed underground. We trench from the house to the building and run the feeder in conduit at the required depth, sized for the load and the distance. For a shed that only needs light and a couple of outlets, a single circuit may be enough. For a garage or workshop, we install a subpanel with its own grounding electrode and a disconnect, which the code requires for a separate building.

Inside the Building

We install lighting, outlets and the circuits you need, with GFCI protection on garage and shed outlets. Bright LED fixtures make a big difference; see garage lighting installation. For car charging in a detached garage, we size the feeder to include it; see EV charger installation. We use wiring methods suited to unfinished spaces and damp locations.

Attached Garages

Attached garages often need more outlets, better lighting and a dedicated circuit or two. The work is simpler because the panel is usually close.

What Affects the Cost

The distance and route for the trench, the size of the feeder, and what you want inside the building are the main factors. We'll tell you if anything like a driveway or patio is in the way.

Garage Lighting

Most garages start with one bare bulb. We replace it with bright, even LED shop lighting on a switch by the door, and add outlets and circuits for tools, freezers and workbenches.

Barn Wiring

Horse barns and pole buildings need more than a garage: a properly sized feeder and subpanel, damp- and dust-rated lighting, GFCI-protected outlets, and circuits for water heaters, fans and heated waterers. We also replace old barn wiring that's been added onto for decades.

Garage and Shed Wiring Around Yardley

We run power to detached garages and workshops on larger lots in Washington Crossing and Quakertown, and to backyard sheds in Levittown.
faq:
How deep does wiring to a shed need to be buried?

It depends on the wiring method and conduit. We follow the code depth for the method we use and call to have utilities marked first.

Does a detached garage need its own panel?

Not always. A small shed can run on one circuit; a garage or workshop usually benefits from a subpanel.

Do I need a permit?

Yes. Running power to a detached building needs a permit and an inspection.

title: Electric Car Charger Installation
h1: EV Charger Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: EV Charger Installation in Yardley, PA | Level 2 Chargers in Bucks County
seoDescription: Level 2 EV charger installation in Yardley, PA by a Tesla-certified installer. Tesla, Rivian, Kia, Ford and more. Load calculation, permit and testing included.
intro: A Level 2 charger adds roughly 25 to 30 miles of range per hour, enough to fill most EVs overnight. We're certified by Tesla to install their Level 2 chargers, and we install chargers for every major brand in garages and driveways around Yardley.
summary: Level 2 home EV charger installation by a Tesla-certified installer. We check your panel's capacity, run the circuit to your garage or driveway, and install and test chargers for Tesla, Rivian, Ford, Kia and other brands.
imageAlt: Measuring load at the electrical panel with a clamp meter
signsTitle: Is Your Home Ready for a Level 2 Charger?
signsList:
• You're charging from a regular 120-volt outlet and it can't keep up
  • You have a 100 amp service, or your panel is nearly full
  • The garage is detached, or the charger needs to go outside
  • You have two EVs, or plan to
  • You want a charger on the same circuit as a future second car
body:
How We Install Your Charger

Every install starts with a load calculation. A charger is a large, continuous load, and we need to confirm your service can carry it along with your heat, air conditioning, cooking and water heater. Most homes with a 200 amp service can add a charger with no trouble. If yours can't, we'll explain your options, from load-management devices to a panel upgrade.

Then we install a dedicated circuit sized for the charger, typically 40 to 60 amps at 240 volts, and run it to where you park. Wire runs are neat and protected, inside the garage or outdoors in conduit. We mount the charger, configure it for the circuit, and test it with your car. The job is permitted and inspected.

Chargers We Install

We're certified by Tesla to install the Tesla Wall Connector, and we install hardwired and plug-in chargers from ChargePoint, Emporia, Grizzl-E, Wallbox and the automakers themselves for Rivian, Ford, Kia, Hyundai, Mercedes, BYD and more. We can install a NEMA 14-50 outlet if you'd rather plug in a mobile charger.

What Affects the Cost

The distance from the panel to the charger, whether the run is inside or outside, the charger's amperage and your panel's capacity all affect the price. Detached garages may need a trench or a garage subpanel.

Choosing Where to Mount the Charger

We'll look at where you park, where the charge port is on your car and whether you might add a second EV later. Mounting the charger where the cable reaches comfortably without crossing a walkway keeps it safe and convenient. Outdoor chargers need a location that's protected from snow piles and plows, and the charger itself must be rated for outdoor use.

EV Chargers Around Yardley

We install chargers in garages throughout Newtown, Warrington and Richboro, and in driveways on the larger lots around Washington Crossing.
faq:
Do I need a permit for an EV charger?

Yes. A new 240-volt circuit for a charger needs a permit and an inspection, which we handle for you.

Should I hardwire the charger or use an outlet?

Hardwiring is more reliable and allows higher charging speeds. A NEMA 14-50 outlet is more flexible if you might change chargers.

Can my 100 amp panel handle an EV charger?

Sometimes, with a lower-amperage charger or a load-management device. The load calculation tells us for sure.

h1: Recessed Lighting Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Recessed Lighting Installation in Yardley, PA | Can Lights in Bucks County
seoDescription: Recessed lighting installation in Yardley, PA. Slim LED wafer and can lights for kitchens, living rooms and basements, laid out evenly and on dimmers.
intro: Recessed lighting is the most requested lighting upgrade we do in Yardley. Done well, it makes a room look bigger, brighter and cleaner. Done badly, it looks like a runway. We plan the layout, pick the right fixtures and install them cleanly in finished ceilings.
summary: Recessed LED lighting for kitchens, living rooms, basements and baths, laid out for even light without dark spots or glare, on dimmers, and installed in finished ceilings with minimal patching.
imageAlt: Ryan Huck installing a slim LED recessed light in a finished ceiling
signsTitle: Good Rooms for Recessed Lighting
signsList:
• Kitchens that rely on one center fixture
  • Living and family rooms without overhead lighting
  • Basements with low ceilings
  • Hallways and stairwells
  • Bathrooms and showers (with wet-rated fixtures)
body:
Planning the Layout

Good recessed lighting starts on paper. We space fixtures based on ceiling height and the room's use, keep them the right distance from walls so they wash the walls instead of leaving scallops, and line them up with cabinets, islands and furniture. We'll suggest color temperature (warmer for living spaces, a little cooler for kitchens and work areas) and zone the lights so they're controlled in useful groups.

Fixtures That Fit Your Ceiling

Modern slim LED "wafer" lights need very little ceiling depth, which makes them ideal for basements and for ceilings with joists or ductwork in the way. Where there's attic insulation above, fixtures must be IC-rated for contact with insulation and airtight so they don't leak heated or cooled air. Over tubs and showers, we use fixtures rated for wet locations.

Clean Installation in Finished Ceilings

Most of our recessed lighting jobs are in finished rooms. We cut the holes precisely, fish wire between fixtures through the ceiling from the attic or from below, and leave little or no patching. Every layout goes on a dimmer matched to the fixtures, so the lights dim smoothly without flicker. If you already have old cans, see LED lighting retrofits. For a single decorative fixture, see ceiling light installation.

What Affects the Cost

The number of lights, ceiling access, the type of fixture and how many switching zones you want drive the price. A kitchen might need 6 to 10 lights; a large basement more.

Retrofit vs. New Construction Fixtures

In existing ceilings, we use remodel-style fixtures that install through the hole without access from above. In new construction or open ceilings, new-construction housings attach to the framing. Both look the same when finished; the choice depends on your ceiling.

Recessed Lighting Around Yardley

We install recessed lighting in kitchens and family rooms throughout Bensalem and Newtown, and in basement finishes in Southampton.
faq:
How many recessed lights do I need?

It depends on the room size, ceiling height and use. As a starting point, many rooms space lights roughly four to six feet apart. We lay it out for your room.

Can you install recessed lights without an attic above?

Yes. Slim LED wafer lights and careful wire fishing let us install them in first-floor and basement ceilings.

What color temperature should I choose?

Around 2700K to 3000K feels warm and suits living spaces. 3500K to 4000K is crisper for kitchens and work areas.

h1: Light Fixture Installation in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Light Fixture Installation in Yardley, PA | Chandeliers, Pendants & Sconces
seoDescription: Light fixture installation in Yardley, PA: ceiling lights, chandeliers, pendants, wall sconces and track lighting, safely supported and wired. Free estimates.
intro: A new light fixture is one of the fastest ways to change how a room looks. We install every kind of fixture in Yardley-area homes, from a simple flush mount to a two-story foyer chandelier, and we make sure the box, the support and the wiring behind it are right.
summary: Ceiling lights, chandeliers, pendants, wall sconces and track lighting, installed level, at the right height and on a box rated for the weight. We add new boxes and switches where there's no fixture today.
imageAlt: Hanging a crystal chandelier from a stepladder
signsTitle: When to Call an Electrician
signsList:

  • A room has only a switched outlet and no ceiling light
  • You want a light where there's no box, like over an island or beside a mirror
  • The existing box is loose, or the wires are brittle or scorched
  • The fixture goes on a high or sloped ceiling
body:
Ceiling Lights

We remove the old fixture, check the box and wiring, and fix what isn't right: a loose or undersized box, wire insulation made brittle by years of heat, or a missing ground. Many older bedrooms and living rooms have a switched outlet instead of a ceiling light, so we run a new switch leg through the attic or from below and install a properly supported box. Replacing every builder-grade fixture in one visit is efficient and gives the house a consistent look.

Chandeliers

A chandelier needs a box and support rated for its weight, and it has to hang at the right height: about 30 to 36 inches above a dining table, and high enough to walk under in a foyer. We assemble it, hang it level and put it on a dimmer. For two-story foyers, we bring the ladders and staging to do it safely.

Pendant Lights

Pendants over a kitchen island or peninsula are spaced evenly along its length and hung so they light the counter without blocking the view across the room. We add boxes where they're needed, use adapters for sloped ceilings and put the pendants on their own switch or dimmer.

Wall Sconces

Sconces beside a bathroom mirror light your face evenly, without the shadows an overhead light casts. We also install them along hallways and stairs, beside the bed and at exterior doors, fishing new boxes into finished walls at the right height.

Track Lighting

Modern LED track and monorail lighting lets you aim light at artwork, a kitchen work area or a display, and move the heads later. It works well on sloped ceilings, where recessed lights can be hard to fit.

What Affects the Cost

Straight swaps are quick, especially several in one visit. New boxes and switch legs, high ceilings, heavy fixtures and chandeliers that need a lot of assembly take longer. Your written estimate covers all of it before any work starts.

Light Fixtures Around Yardley

We replace dated fixtures in older homes in Levittown and Bristol, and hang chandeliers and pendants in remodeled kitchens and foyers in Newtown and Doylestown.

Usually 30 to 36 inches above the tabletop, a little higher with taller ceilings. We'll set it where it looks and works best.

We can, or we'll install the one you've chosen.

seoTitle: Under Cabinet Lighting Installation in Yardley, PA | Bucks County Kitchens
seoDescription: Under cabinet lighting installation in Yardley, PA. Hardwired LED light bars and strips on a wall switch, hidden wiring and drivers. Licensed electricians.
intro: Overhead lights leave shadows on your counters, right where you're working. Under-cabinet lighting fixes that and makes the whole kitchen look finished. We install hardwired LED under-cabinet lighting in Yardley-area kitchens, on a wall switch, with no cords showing.
summary: Hardwired LED under-cabinet lighting on a wall switch or dimmer, with the wiring and drivers hidden, so your counters are evenly lit without cords or dark spots.
signsTitle: Signs You Need Under-Cabinet Lighting
signsList:
• You work in your own shadow at the counter
  • The backsplash disappears in the evening
  • Old puck lights run hot or have burned out
  • Plug-in lights leave cords hanging into the outlets
  • You're remodeling and want it planned in
body:
Choosing the Fixtures

Slim LED light bars give even light with no hot spots and install neatly at the front of the cabinet. LED strip lighting in an aluminum channel with a diffuser works well for a continuous line. Old-style puck lights create pools of light and are best for accents. We'll help you choose the color temperature to match your other lights and the brightness for your counters.

Hardwired and Hidden

We run power from a nearby circuit into the cabinets and to a wall switch, often fishing the wire behind the backsplash or through the cabinets. Low-voltage systems need a driver, which we hide in a cabinet where it can still be reached. Everything goes on a switch or dimmer, sometimes with the pendants or on a separate control. In a remodel, we rough in the wiring before the backsplash goes up.

Part of a Kitchen Lighting Plan

Under-cabinet lighting works best as one layer of a plan: recessed lights for general light, pendants over the island, and under-cabinet lights for tasks. See kitchen electrical upgrades for circuits, outlets and appliances.

What Affects the Cost

Linear feet of cabinets, fixture type, whether walls and backsplash are finished and where the switch goes all shape the price.

Placement and Color

Mounting fixtures toward the front edge of the cabinet lights the counter rather than the backsplash, and reduces reflections on shiny counters. Warm or neutral color temperatures usually match the kitchen's other lighting best. If your counters are polished stone, we'll choose fixtures with diffused lenses so you don't see a row of reflected dots. For glass-front cabinets, a separate strip inside the cabinet shows off what's on display. We can put those on their own switch or dimmer.

LED Strip Lighting

Hardwired LED strip lighting in aluminum channels with diffusers gives an even line of light with no visible dots. We use it in coves, cabinets, shelves, stairs, bars and toe-kicks, with drivers sized for the run and tucked out of sight.

Cove and Accent Lighting

Soft light in a tray ceiling or along crown molding, or accent light on shelves, artwork and built-ins, makes a room feel finished. We hide the drivers and put everything on a dimmer.

Under-Cabinet Lighting Around Yardley

We install under-cabinet lighting in kitchen remodels in Doylestown and Feasterville, and add it to existing kitchens in Langhorne.
faq:
Can under-cabinet lights be added to an existing kitchen?

Yes. We fish power into the cabinets and add a switch, usually without disturbing the backsplash much.

Hardwired or plug-in?

Hardwired is cleaner, runs on a wall switch and doesn't use up your counter outlets.

Can they be dimmed?

Yes, with dimmable fixtures and a compatible dimmer or driver.

How long do LED under-cabinet lights last?

Quality LED fixtures typically last many years of normal use. Keeping the driver accessible makes it easy to replace if it ever fails.

seoDescription: Security lighting and flood light installation in Yardley, PA. LED floodlights with motion and dusk-to-dawn control for driveways, yards and businesses.
intro: A well-lit property is safer and less inviting to trouble. We install LED flood and security lighting around Yardley-area homes and businesses, with smart controls and careful aiming, so your property is lit without glaring into the neighbors' windows.
summary: LED floodlights and security lighting for driveways, yards, entrances and commercial lots, with motion sensors, dusk-to-dawn control and aiming that lights your property without blinding the neighbors.
signsTitle: When to Add Security Lighting
signsList:
• Dark driveways, side yards or back doors
  • Old halogen floods that run hot and burn out
  • Cameras that can't see at night
  • A detached garage, barn or shed with no outdoor light
  • A business lot or entrance that needs to be lit after hours
body:
Choosing the Right Lights

LED floodlights use far less power than old halogen fixtures and last much longer. We choose brightness and beam spread for the area, and color temperature that looks good and helps cameras. Many homes pair a floodlight at the driveway with motion sensor lighting at the doors.

Controls

Security lights can run dusk-to-dawn with a photocell, turn on with motion, or both: dim all night and full brightness on motion. They can also be scheduled or controlled from your phone with smart switches. We set the controls to match how you use your property.

Aiming and Mounting

We mount fixtures high enough to cover the area and aim them down, which lights your property effectively and keeps glare out of the neighbors' windows and drivers' eyes. Fixtures on older homes, detached buildings and barns may need new wiring and boxes. Runs to detached buildings go underground in conduit.

Beyond Security

For lighting that makes the yard look good, see landscape lighting. For outlets for holiday lights and tools, see outdoor outlet installation.

What Affects the Cost

Replacing existing floods is quick. New locations, high mounting, brick or stone walls and runs to detached buildings take more time.

Lighting and Cameras

Cameras record much better with good lighting. Floodlights that come on with motion give cameras clear, color footage instead of grainy night vision. Some combined camera-floodlight units need a strong mounting point and steady power; we'll install the box and wiring they need. We can also add outlets or power for standalone cameras near the lights, so everything is powered and nothing depends on batteries.

Motion Sensor Lighting

Motion lights at the driveway, doors and walkways come on when you need them and save energy the rest of the time. Indoors, occupancy and vacancy sensor switches are handy in closets, laundry rooms, garages and stairways.

Security Lighting Around Yardley

We install floodlights and security lighting on driveways and yards in Quakertown and Washington Crossing, and on commercial buildings in Bensalem.

Can floodlights be on a motion sensor and a timer?

Yes. Many fixtures run dim all night and go to full brightness on motion.

How do I keep floodlights from bothering neighbors?

Mount them high and aim them down at your property. We choose fixtures with good glare control.

Are LED floodlights bright enough?

Yes. They're brighter than halogen per watt and last years longer.

Can you replace old halogen floodlights?

Yes. We replace them with LED fixtures that use far less power, run cooler and last much longer, often on the same box.

seoTitle: Landscape Lighting Installation in Yardley, PA | Outdoor Lighting, Bucks County
seoDescription: Landscape and low-voltage lighting installation in Yardley, PA. LED path lights, uplights, patio and step lighting with transformers and timers.
intro: Landscape lighting makes a home look inviting after dark and makes paths and steps safer. We design and install low-voltage LED landscape lighting around Yardley-area homes, from a few path lights to the whole property.
summary: Low-voltage LED landscape lighting for paths, driveways, trees, steps, patios and the front of the house, with properly sized transformers, buried cable and timers or astronomical clocks.
signsTitle: What Landscape Lighting Can Light
signsList:
• Walkways, driveways and steps
  • Trees, shrubs and garden beds (uplighting)

  • Patios, decks and outdoor kitchens

body:
Low-Voltage Systems

Most landscape lighting runs on 12 volts from a transformer plugged into or wired to a GFCI-protected outdoor outlet. Low voltage is safer around the yard and lets fixtures be moved as plants grow. We size the transformer for the total load with room to add fixtures, plan cable runs to keep brightness even, and bury cable neatly so it doesn't get cut by edgers or aerators. If you need a new outlet for the transformer, see outdoor outlet installation.

Designing the Layout

Good landscape lighting lights what matters and leaves some darkness for contrast. We walk the property with you, usually at dusk, and plan path lights, uplights on trees and walls, and step and deck lights. Warm LED color temperature looks best on stone, brick and plants. We aim fixtures to avoid glare into windows and neighboring yards.

Timers and Controls

Transformers with photocells and timers, or astronomical clocks that follow sunset through the seasons, keep lights running without you touching them. Smart transformers can be controlled from your phone. For motion-activated or brighter lighting, see security and flood lighting. Around pools, low-voltage lighting follows specific rules; see pool electrical wiring.

What Affects the Cost

The number of fixtures, the fixture quality, the size of the property and how the cable is routed drive the price. Many homeowners start with the front and add more later.

Fixture Quality Matters

Landscape fixtures live outdoors year-round, so materials matter. Solid brass and copper fixtures last far longer than painted aluminum or plastic and develop a natural patina. Sealed LED fixtures resist moisture and insects. Quality connectors keep water out of connections, which is the most common cause of failed landscape lighting. We use fixtures and connectors built to last, and we'll show you what to expect from each option.

Maintaining Your System

Plants grow, mulch builds up and fixtures get bumped. An occasional check keeps lights aimed and working, and we can adjust your system as your landscaping changes.

Landscape Lighting Around Yardley

We install landscape lighting on larger properties in Washington Crossing and Richboro, and front-yard and path lighting throughout Newtown.
faq:
Is low-voltage landscape lighting safe?

Yes. It runs on 12 volts from a transformer on a GFCI-protected outlet, which makes it much safer than line-voltage lighting in the yard.

Can I add more lights later?

Yes. We size the transformer with room to expand.

How are the lights controlled?

With a timer, photocell, astronomical clock or smart control, so they come on at dusk automatically.

title: Lighting Repair
h1: Lighting Repair in Yardley, PA
seoTitle: Lighting Repair in Yardley, PA | Flickering Light Repair in Bucks County
seoDescription: Lighting repair in Yardley, PA. Fix flickering or dead lights, buzzing fixtures, failed ballasts, hard-to-reach bulbs and outdoor lights. Licensed electricians.
intro: Lights that flicker, buzz or just stop working are among the most common calls we get. Sometimes it's a bulb; often it's a dimmer, a loose connection or a failing ballast. We repair lighting in Yardley-area homes and businesses and find the real cause.
summary: Fix lights that flicker, buzz or won't turn on, replace failed ballasts and drivers, change bulbs in hard-to-reach fixtures, and repair outdoor and landscape lighting.
signsTitle: Lighting Problems We Fix
signsList:
• Lights that flicker or pulse, on a dimmer or not
  • Fixtures that buzz or hum
  • Lights that don't turn on, even with a new bulb
  • Fluorescent fixtures that flicker, hum or won't light
  • Bulbs in high ceilings, foyers and stairwells you can't reach
  • Outdoor, porch and landscape lights that have quit
body:
Finding the Cause

Flicker has many causes: an incompatible dimmer, a loose connection at the fixture or switch, a failing LED driver or a worn socket. Flicker across several rooms can point to a loose connection at the panel or service, which needs attention soon; see electrical repair and troubleshooting. We test the circuit, the switch and the fixture to find the cause, then fix it.

Ballast and Bulb Replacement

Fluorescent fixtures use a ballast that eventually fails, causing flicker, humming or dark tubes. We can replace the ballast, but in many cases converting the fixture to LED makes more sense; see LED lighting retrofits. We also replace bulbs in fixtures that are hard or unsafe to reach, like two-story foyers, cathedral ceilings and stairwells, and can switch them to long-life LEDs so you won't need us again for years.

Outdoor and Landscape Lights

Outdoor fixtures face weather, and moisture causes corrosion and failures. We repair and replace porch lights, floodlights, post lights and landscape lighting, and fix tripped or failed transformers and photocells.

What Affects the Cost

Most lighting repairs are quick once the cause is found. High ceilings, several fixtures and replacement parts affect the price, which we'll give you before doing the work.

When to Replace Instead of Repair

If a fixture has corroded sockets, brittle wiring from years of heat, or cracked housings, replacing it is often cheaper than repairing it. Older fixtures in closets and attics may lack the protection that modern fixtures have. We'll tell you when a repair makes sense and when a new fixture is the better value, and give you prices for both.

LED Retrofits

If your fixtures are old fluorescents, halogens or recessed cans, an LED retrofit often costs less over time than repairing them. We bypass ballasts, install LED retrofit kits or replace fixtures outright, in homes and small businesses.

Lighting Repair Around Yardley

We fix flickering and failed lighting throughout Bristol, Morrisville and Perkasie.
faq:
Why do my lights flicker?

Usually a loose bulb, an incompatible dimmer, a loose connection or a failing driver. Flicker in several rooms can mean a problem at the panel.

Should I replace my fluorescent ballast or switch to LED?

If the fixture is in good shape, either works. LED conversion usually costs about the same and ends ballast failures for good.

Can you change bulbs in my two-story foyer?

Yes. We bring the equipment to work safely at height and can switch you to long-life LEDs.

Why does my light bulb keep burning out?

Common causes are a loose socket, too much heat in an enclosed fixture, voltage problems or the wrong bulb type. We check the fixture and circuit to find it.
